n: the cardinal number that is the sum of seven and one

d: Etym: [Gr. “A poem of eight lines. [Obs.] Selden”
1. (Arch.) “A molding, the section of which is the form of the letter S, with the convex part above; cyma reversa. See Illust. under Cyma.”
2. Hence, any similar figure used for any purpose. Ogee arch (Arch.), a pointed arch, each of the sides of which has the curve of an ogee, that is, has a reversed curve near the apex.
w.e: F. ogive, augive, LL. augiva, of uncertain origin; cf.LL. ogis a support, prop. L. augere to increase, strengthen, Sp. auge highest point of power or fortune, apogee, Ar. auj, an astronomical term.

n: a molding that (in section) has the shape of an S with the convex part above and the concave part below

d: olive-shaped, drupaceous fruit of a species of tupelo (Nyssa capitata) which grows in swamps in Georgia and Florida. (b) The tree which bears this fruit.

w.e: L.oggannire to snarl at; ob (see Ob-) + gannire to yelp.

d: A particular kind of writing practiced by the ancient Irish, and found in inscriptions on stones, metals, etc. [Written also ogam.]

w.e: F. ogive, OF. augive a pointed arch, LL. augiva a double arch of two at right angles.

n: front consisting of the conical head of a missile or rocket that protects the payload from heat during its passage through the atmosphere

d: To view or look at with side glances, as in fondness, or with a design to attract notice. And ogling all their audience, ere they speak. Dryden.
w.e: From a Dutch word corresponding to G. äugeln to ogle, fr. auge eye; cf. D. ooglonken to ogle, OD. oogen to cast sheep's eyes upon, ooge eye. See Eye.

d: An amorous side glance or look. Byron.

n: a viewer who gives a flirtatious or lewd look at another person

d: An imaginary monster, or hideous giant of fairy tales, who lived on human beings; hence, any frightful giant; a cruel monster. His schoolroom must have resembled an ogre's den. Maccaulay.
w.e: F., fr. Sp. ogro, fr. L. Orcus the god of the infernal regions; also, the lower world, hell.

n: (folklore) a giant who likes to eat human beings
a cruel wicked and inhuman person

d: Resembling an ogre; having the character or appearance of an ogre; suitable for an ogre. An ogreish kind of jocularity. Dickens.
Ogre*ism, n. “The character or manners of an ogre.”
Ogre*ism, n. “The character or manners of an ogre.”
Etym: [L. Ogygius, Gr. “Of or pertaining to Ogyges, a mythical king of ancient Attica, or to a great deluge in Attica in his days; hence, primeval; of obscure antiquity.”
